hints.title: Odd Parity Character Count
hints.text: A string can be rearranged into a palindrome if at most one character has an odd frequency. Each replacement can eliminate two odd counts.

hints.title: Prefix Parity Bitmask
hints.text: Encode character parity up to each index using an integer bitmask where the c-th bit toggles on each appearance.

hints.title: Range Query Parity Check
hints.text: The odd character count in range [left, right] equals popcount(prefix[right + 1] ^ prefix[left]). The query is feasible if and only if odd_count // 2 <= k.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def canMakePaliQueries(self, s: str, queries: list[list[int]]) -> list[bool]:
        n = len(s)
        prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i, c in enumerate(s):
            prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] ^ (1 << (ord(c) - ord('a')))
        
        res = []
        for left, right, k in queries:
            mask = prefix[right + 1] ^ prefix[left]
            odd_cnt = bin(mask).count('1')
            res.append(odd_cnt // 2 <= k)
        return res
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning substring ranges for each query takes O(N * Q) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Prefix parity masks allow answering any query in O(1) bitwise operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that palindrome rearrangement only cares about character parities, which can be queried via prefix XOR masks.
complexity.notes: Each replacement can repair 2 odd parity counts.
